tasks.title: University learning analytics policy
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: Your class has listened to a radio discussion about how universities should manage the data generated by digital study tools such as adaptive learning platforms and automated feedback systems. You have made the notes below.

promptBlocks.heading: Priorities for a university learning analytics policy
listItems: ensuring student data is anonymised and secure
giving students access to their own learning data
using analytics to identify students who need extra support

promptBlocks.heading: Some opinions expressed in the discussion:
paragraphs: If student data isn't properly anonymised, it could be misused by employers or insurers. Security has to come first.
Students should be able to see their own data – it helps them take control of their learning and builds trust in the system.
The whole point of analytics is to help struggling students early. Without that, it's just surveillance.

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay for your tutor discussing two of the priorities in your notes. You should explain which priority you think is more important for universities to address, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

tasks.title: Proposal for a learning analytics framework
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: Your university is developing a framework for the ethical use of learning analytics. The vice-chancellor has invited proposals from students for how this framework should be designed.

Write a proposal for the vice-chancellor. In your proposal, you should:
• recommend two specific principles that should govern the use of student data
• explain how these principles would benefit both students and the institution
• suggest how the university could ensure compliance with the framework

tasks.title: Responding to a programme coordinator
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Learning analytics pilot – your views
paragraphs: As you know, the university is planning a pilot programme that would give all first-year students access to a personalised learning dashboard, showing their progress, predicted grades and areas for improvement. Some staff have raised concerns that this might increase anxiety among students and lead to unfair comparisons.

I would like to hear your views on this initiative. Please write back explaining your position on the proposed dashboard, analysing one potential drawback of the pilot, and proposing a way to address that drawback while still moving forward.

tasks.title: Review of a learning analytics tool
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Learning analytics tools
paragraphs: Have you used a learning analytics tool – for example, a dashboard that tracks your grades, a platform that predicts your performance, or an app that recommends study resources based on your progress?
We want to hear about your experience. Write a review for our student advice website.
Describe the tool and what it does. Evaluate how well it balances personalised support with respect for your privacy and autonomy. Would you recommend it to other students? Why or why not?
The best reviews will be published on our website.
